Welcome

David, here are the homes I picked out for you.

I'm glad to be helping you with the move. I put this page together so you can get a feel for the different parts of Costa Rica and the kind of home your budget buys in each one.

I sent you a wide range on purpose, including a few homes above your budget and some that are still being built, so you can get a real feel for the market here and what each price point buys. There are a lot of properties, and you don't need to study every one. Think of this first round as a way for me to learn your taste. Once I know what you're drawn to, I'll narrow it down to a short list that's worth flying down for.

  1. 1
    Start with the areasEach section opens with a short intro to the area. If one clearly isn't for you, skip it.
  2. 2
    Note what catches your eyeGo with your gut. A great kitchen or a big lawn is reason enough.
  3. 3
    Tell me what you likeSend me the homes that stand out, with a line on what you liked and what you didn't. That helps me narrow things down quickly.

Tiago

A note on price

List prices here are a starting point.

Costa Rica is a very negotiable market. Most sellers expect offers below the asking price, and there is usually real room to work with.

That's why I included a few homes at or slightly over $5M. Don't rule a home out because of its list price. If you love it, let me handle the negotiation.

Area 1 of 6 · 10 homes

Reserva Conchal

Gated golf and beach resort above Playa Conchal

The most polished community in the area. A Robert Trent Jones II golf course runs through it, with a private Beach Club on Playa Conchal, the Westin and W hotels, tennis, trails and 24/7 security. The homes here are mostly brand new, built in neighborhoods like Sauco, Laurel, Ceibo and Sanara.

To Liberia airport
About 1 hr
Beaches
Playa Conchal + Beach Club
For the dog
Lots run about a third of an acre, with quiet streets and trails inside the gates.

Area 2 of 6 · 10 homes

Hacienda Pinilla

4,500-acre gated resort with three miles of coastline

A private resort community south of Tamarindo with a championship golf course, a Beach Club on Playa Avellanas, the JW Marriott, an equestrian center and around 40 km of trails. Homes sit in quiet sub-communities like Las Golondrinas, Los Almendros and Coralis, and lots tend to be larger than anywhere else in a gated setting. Tamarindo is about 15 minutes away.

To Liberia airport
About 1 hr 30 min
Beaches
Avellanas, Playa Bonita, Langosta
For the dog
Half-acre lots are common, and the trail network is ideal for long walks.

Mar Vista, Flamingo & Potrero

Hillside ocean views above Flamingo Bay

The hills above Flamingo Bay have some of the best ocean views on this coast, with the marina, restaurants and several beaches a few minutes away. Mar Vista is a gated community on the ridge with lots of an acre or more, plus a restaurant, gym, tennis and pickleball. Potrero is a quieter beach village just to the north.

Tamarindo

The main beach town, with gated hillside communities above it

Tamarindo has the most restaurants, shops and services in the area, and a lively beach. El Tesoro and Tamarindo Park are gated communities on the hill right above town, with views across the bay to Playa Grande. Senderos and La Colina de Culebras are a few minutes outside town and a little more private.

Area 5 of 6 · 6 homes

Playa Grande

Protected beach inside Las Baulas National Marine Park

Just across the estuary from Tamarindo, but much quieter. The beach is part of a national park where leatherback turtles nest, so development stays low and the coastline stays natural. Las Ventanas is a 380-acre gated community on the hills with a clubhouse, trails and courts, and Corona del Cabo sits a few minutes inland.

To Liberia airport
About 1 hr 10 min
Beaches
Playa Grande, Playa Ventanas
For the dog
Generous lots with forest and trails around them.

Area 6 of 6 · 7 properties

Inland: Arenal, Monteverde & Bijagua

More land, cooler air and volcano country

The interior is a different side of Costa Rica. Arenal has the volcano, the lake and the hot springs around La Fortuna. Monteverde is cloud forest at altitude with a cool, spring-like climate all year. Bijagua sits between the Tenorio and Miravalles volcanoes near the Río Celeste. Your money buys far more land here, with longer drives to the beach and airport.

To Liberia airport
About 1 hr 20 min to 3 hrs
Beaches
Coast is 1.5 to 3 hrs
For the dog
All the room in the world to roam.
Price range here
$950K to $3M

Reply with the homes that stood out and a few words on why. A style you liked, a home that felt too big, an area that sounds right. From there I'll put together a short list, set up private showings for your visit, and handle the negotiation once you find the one.
